description: The design system's widget primitives. A spec picks one primitive, maps its result columns to the primitive's roles and may set a few design intents. Rendering, colors and spacing come from the app; a spec never styles anything - an intent names what matters, the app decides how it looks.

number.description: Number with grouping, up to 2 decimals.

percent.description: A 0-1 ratio shown as a percent.

percentPoints.description: A 0-100 value shown as a percent.

date.description: Short date, e.g. Oct 16, 2026. A column with a grain shows its period instead: Sep 2026, 2026 Q3, 2026.

badge.description: A colored tag; tones map values to good | warn | bad | info | neutral.

asOfDate.description: The dataset's 'today' (_meta.asOfDate). Declare it and use {"$param": "asOfDate"} for YTD, trailing-12-month and 'last N quarters' logic. Never use $$NOW.

intents.emphasis: Which mark the eye goes to: latest (the most recent period - trends), max or min (the leader or laggard - rankings), none (all marks equal - when no single row is the story). The emphasized mark keeps the accent color and carries its value; the rest are muted.
intents.polarity: Whether a rise is good: higherIsBetter (revenue, deposits, pipeline, headroom), lowerIsBetter (utilization, exposure at risk, overdue items, risk signals), neutral (no judgement). Colors every change: a rise that is bad shows red.
intents.headline: The figure a bar or line card leads with, computed from the rows by the app: latest (last period, with its change vs the one before), total (sum over the rows - only for additive units USD and count), average, change (last vs first), none.
intents.reference: A numeric column drawn as a limit, target or maximum, in the same unit as the values it is compared with (e.g. committedUsd behind drawnUsd).

metric.description: One headline number, optionally compared with another (shown as a % change, colored by polarity) and with a secondary figure underneath. With x, a short history: the last row is the value, the row before is the comparison, and every row draws a sparkline.

compare.description: Prior-period value; the change vs value is shown as a percent.

secondary.description: A supporting figure shown under the value with its column label.

x.description: Set it to show a sparkline: the period of each row, ascending.

metric.guidance: Use for a single KPI. Without x the pipeline ends in exactly one row ($group with _id: null). With x it returns one row per period (12 closed months is typical), sorted ascending - only when the data was built that way.

meter.description: A value against its maximum, as a progress bar: utilization of a limit, share of wallet, covenant headroom. With x, one labelled meter per row.

reference.description: The maximum (a limit or total, same unit as value). Leave it out when value is a 0-1 ratio.

secondary.description: A supporting figure under the bar (single meter only).

x.description: Row label, for one meter per row (e.g. per facility).

options.warnAt: number 0-1: the fraction of the maximum where the bar turns to warning (at or above it for lowerIsBetter, at or below for higherIsBetter)

meter.guidance: Use when the question is 'how much of the limit / the whole is used'. value is a ratio (unit ratio) or has a reference in the same unit. Set polarity and warnAt when a level is a concern (utilization: lowerIsBetter, warnAt 0.8).

bar.description: Compare a number across categories, or across a handful of periods. One horizontal series is drawn as a ranked bar list.

y.description: One or more series, all in the same unit.

reference.description: A limit or target per row, same unit as y, drawn as a dashed mark.

series.description: Long-format rows: one series per value of this column (e.g. one line per line of business), with exactly one y column. The renderer pivots them; at most 4 series.

bar.guidance: Use horizontal for long category names and rankings. Sort the rows in the pipeline; the chart keeps their order. Prefer line for long time series. Periods: emphasis latest and a headline. Rankings: emphasis max (or none). Emphasis and headline apply to the first series.

line.description: Show how numbers move over time. One series is drawn over a soft area with its latest value labelled.

y.description: One or more series, all in the same unit.

reference.description: A limit or target per period, same unit as y, drawn as a dashed line.

series.description: Long-format rows: one series per value of this column (e.g. one line per line of business), with exactly one y column. The renderer pivots them; at most 4 series.

line.guidance: One row per period, sorted ascending. Pivot categories into columns (one y column per series) rather than returning long-format rows. A headline (latest or total) gives the card its number.

composition.description: Parts of a whole: one 100% bar of segments and a list of each part's value and share, led by the total.

y.description: Exactly one non-negative, additive column (USD or count).

composition.guidance: Use for mix and share questions (revenue by line of business, deposit mix). Sort the parts largest first in the pipeline. Past six parts the rest fold into Other.

table.description: Rows of records with mixed columns.
table.guidance: Sort and $limit in the pipeline. Use format badge with tones for status columns.

list.description: A compact feed of items: a tone dot, title, subtitle, a badge and a meta value on the right.

badge.description: Give it badge tones: they also color the item's dot.

list.guidance: Use for signals, contacts, activities. Sort and $limit in the pipeline.

columnFeatures.grain: A date column with grain month, quarter or year holds the first day of each period and is shown as that period.
columnFeatures.unitFrom: {column, map}: the unit varies per row and is read from another column (covenant actual and limit are x, % or USD); each value is formatted in its own unit.
columnFeatures.hidden: Carried for another column or for linking (e.g. a client id beside its name), not shown in tables.
